messages:
maria (pm): quick kickoff — we're scoping the 'upgrade runways' work for private deploys (vpc/onprem). primary goals: reinstall-free upgrades, a light connector shim for customer-managed networking, clear launch acceptance criteria. 11am sync?

devon (eng-plat): +1. i'd like to align on what 'reinstall-free' means technically — operator shim + versioned CRD rollout? also need a compatibility matrix for host OS, k8s, and kernel modules.

sarah (field): customers keep asking for zero-tenant downtime and preserved egress ips. acme corp specifically called out SNAT-preservation or deterministic egress mapping. this is high priority for a pilot.

oleg (netops): proposal: split into two connector modes — 'managed-tunnel' (redwood-controlled dataplane) and 'connector-shim' (customer runs a small reverse-proxy/agent). connector-shim constraints: must work with strict outbound-only firewalls and no inbound ports.

kevin (security): important: any connector-shim must support customer KMS/HSM for keys or never persist control-plane tokens. require auditable rotation. add to acceptance criteria.

maria (pm): agreed. i'll draft acceptance checklist. rough one below — feedback pls: 
```
- rolling upgrade with no tenant ejection or forced reprovisioning
- preserved/explicit egress mapping or documented migration path
- connector-shim operates outbound-only, <1MB memory footprint target
- operator/CRD supports canary -> stable rollouts and fast rollback
- audit logs surfaced to customer SIEM, KMS-integrated secrets
- automated health checks + smoke tests (per customer)
```

devon (eng-plat): looks good. add: a migration verifier that runs post-upgrade to validate model-compatibility (embedding dims, tokenizer). could be a mini-eval: `redwood-upgrade-check --suite basic-latency`

oleg (netops): one more note — some customers will not allow any new NAT ranges. we need a mapping plan: either preserve original IPs (hard) or support IP-mapping gateway that sits in-customer-network. document both fallback lanes.

sarah (field): timeline ask from field: pilot with 2 customers in Q2, GA by end of Q3. pilots require rollback playbook and runbooks for netops.

kevin (security): add threat-modeling session to the pilot prep. flag for legal: data plane termination points and PII handling during migration.

maria (pm): planning notes:
- next steps: devon/oleg to produce proposed connector API + failure modes by EOD Tue
- kevin to own security checklist and threat modeling slot for Wed
- sarah to line up pilot customers and list acceptance test suites
- i'll collate into a launch gate doc and share link: <https://go/redwood/priv-upgrade>

devon (eng-plat): i'll toss a PoC repo with operator shim + demo CR for review. ETA Thu.

deploy-bot: meeting scheduled: private-upgrade-kickoff — Wed 11:00am in #product. Agenda posted. :calendar:

sarah (field): tagging @oleg and @kevin — customer comms will need clear rollback phrasing. avoid 'reinstall' in docs. :sweat_smile:

oleg (netops): noted. i'll draft network rollback appendix: IP-fallback, proxy-patterns, and firewall test checklist.

maria (pm): perfect. if no objections i'll lock this as the working scope for the initiative and surface priorities in next WG. :thumbsup:

kevin (security): :+1: from security, except we must add HSM/KMS decision to gating criteria.

devon (eng-plat): +1. also suggest we record perf delta budget (max allowed latency regression) as a numeric gate.

maria (pm): added — perf budget: max 10% p95 token-latency increase after upgrade, otherwise fail gate.

sarah (field): thanks — i'll prep pilot success template to match these gates.

maria (pm): ok closing thread for now, i'll post the doc link and WG invite.
